change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light-theme color of embedded reply author link changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: The old rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new light-theme argument is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, with `$secondary` at 30% for dark. `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument on light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51). So on the default theme this bold author link in `.topic-meta-data h5` becomes much paler. Every other line in this PR keeps the original value and mirrors it for dark themes. The two percentages look swapped. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length: light value changed from 70% to 30%, and the dark value is mirrored the wrong way
findings.body: The old rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. On light themes this hint is now much darker than before. On dark themes it renders `$secondary` at 70%, which is close to the background. The desktop version of the same rule (desktop/modal.scss:94) uses 70% / 30%. Use the same values here.

findings.title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% on light themes
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaces it with 50% / 50%, so on the default theme the name becomes lighter and looks the same as `.title` below it (line 527). The PR body only claims to add dark-theme variants. To keep the light theme unchanged and follow the PR's mirroring convention, use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color changed from 30% to 50% on light themes
findings.body: This is the same issue as desktop/user.scss:522. The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and the new one is 50% / 50%. On light themes the name gets lighter and matches `.title` (line 503). Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile link-summary h3 changed from 20% to 50% on light themes
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new value is 50% / 50%, so on light themes the h3 becomes noticeably lighter and looks like the h4 below it (line 190). The desktop counterpart (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) kept 20% and mirrors it as 80% for dark themes. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

contracts.action: Replace scale-color($primary, X%) with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, X%), scale-color($secondary, 100-X%)) across stylesheets
contracts.before_after: Light themes should get the old value unchanged and dark themes the mirrored $secondary value. Five rules break this: desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497 and mobile/topic-post.scss:182.
contracts.visible_effect: dark-light-choose picks the first argument when $primary is darker than $secondary, so on light themes the rendered text color comes from the first argument.

summary: The PR wraps `scale-color($primary, X%)` in `dark-light-choose(...)` and adds a `$secondary` value for dark themes. Almost every replacement keeps X% on light themes and uses (100−X)% on dark themes, so the default theme looks the same. Five rules break that: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 (30→70, swapped), mobile/modal.scss:102 (70→30, swapped), desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 (30→50) and mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (20→50). Each changes how the light theme looks, which the PR does not describe. embed.css.scss imports foundation/variables, so `dark-light-choose` is defined there.
